title: Token bucket rate limiter
brief:
Build a token bucket rate limiter as a single ES module in TypeScript, targeting Node 20+ with no third-party dependencies.

Export a class `TokenBucket`. Its constructor takes one options object with fields: `capacity` (max tokens held), `refillTokens` (tokens added per interval), `refillIntervalMs` (interval length), and `now` (a zero-argument function returning milliseconds, used for all time reads). Every one of these must have a default drawn from a single named defaults constant declared at the top of the module.

Behaviour:
- `tryRemove(count)` returns true and deducts when enough tokens are available, false and deducts nothing otherwise.
- Refill is lazy: compute elapsed time on each call rather than using a timer.
- The bucket never exceeds `capacity`.
- `available()` returns the current token count after applying pending refill.
- Invalid options (non-positive capacity or interval, negative refill) throw a `RangeError` from the constructor.

The module must not read the system clock directly anywhere except through the injected `now` function, so tests can drive time deterministically.

Write tests using the built-in `node:test` runner and `node:assert/strict`.
acceptance: All four options are configurable and defaulted from one named constant block.
Time is read only through the injected now() function.
Tests drive time deterministically and cover refill, capacity clamping, and the RangeError cases.
